4. It is stated that historically this case property is an important religion Waqf Estate. The property appertaining to CS plots No. 104 and 105 of CS Khatian No. 11148, Touzi No. 3241-B1, CS Sheet No. 19 of Ward No. 16 under Police Station Kotwali, Dhaka including the land, buildings, tanks, gates, compounds, walls together with many tombs and structures thereon belong to Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate, which is a public Waqf having EC No. 11737 (Dhaka). The Hossaini Dalan is an Imambara, which was created and permanently dedicated in the name of God about 350 years ago by Mir Murad, a pious and wealthy Admiral of the Mughal Navy in Bengal, for the public purposes of pious, religious and charitable nature to commemorate the tragic and noble martyrdom of Hazrat Imam Hussain (AS) at Karbala, and has been ever since used, treated and possessed, as such, by the Muslims in general and the members of the Shia community in particular from generation to gene-ration. The Waqf Estate successfully received the patronage and superintendence of the Mughal Emperors, Nawabs and Subedars of Bengal, the East India Company, the Government of India, the Government of Pakistan and finally, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 5. It is also stated that in or about 1844 AD a committee of four Muslim gentlemen including Nawab Khawaja Alimullah, the founder of the Nawab family of Dhaka, was appointed by the Government of India to superintendent the affairs of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. In 1864 another committee of three Muslim gentlemen including Nawab Khawaja Sir Abdul Gani was appointed to look after the affairs of the Imambara. In 1891 the Government appointed Nawab Khawaja Sir Ahsanullah to supervise the affairs of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. After the death of Nawab Khawaja Sir Ahsanullah in 1901, his son Nawab Khawaja Sir Salimullah was appointed to supervise the affairs of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. After his death in 1915, his son Nawab Khawaja Habibullah Bahadur was entrusted with the same task. He being in sole charge of the Waqf Estate since 1916 was also appointed Mutawalli of the same after the Bengal Waqf Act, 1934 came into force. Subsequently, the said Waqf Estate was registered as a public Waqf in the office of the Waqf Commissioner, East Pakistan under EC No. 11737. Late Nawab Khawaja Habibullah Bahadur functioned as Mutawalli of the Estate till he breathed his last on 21-11-1958. Thereafter, the Government of East Pakistan formed a Committee for the management and supervision of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. Justice Ispahani was the Chairman and Nawab Khawaja Hassan Askari and some other leading persons from the Shia Community were the members of the said Committee. After independence of Bangladesh a new Managing Committee was formed with renowned legal expert Mr Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed in the chair. On 30-12-1986 another Managing Committee was formed with Mirza Mehdi Ispahani, in the chair. After his death on 20-1-2004 Mirza Behrooz Ispahani has been appointed the Chairman of the Managing Committee by the Government. Under the guidance and control of the Managing Committee there is a Superintendent to perform his duties of maintenance and management of the Waqf Estate. The petitioner is the present Superintendent of Hossaini Dalan Imambara. 

 6. It is stated that total area of land belonged to Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate appertaining to CS Plots No.104 and 105 is 2.8140 acres. Out of the said quantum of land 1. 9300 acres of land appertaining to CS plot No. 105 is under Khas possession of the Waqf Estate which is known as Hossaini Dalan Building Compound. The other part of the Waqf property comprising an area of 0.8840 acre of land is locally known as 'Gas Garden' and appertaining to CS Plot No. 104 and bounded on all sides by pucca walls and on the south by homestead of Md Yakub, on the north by Hossaini Dalan Road, on the east by pucca compound of Hossaini Dalan and on the west by Hossaini Dalan Road and is hereinafter referred to as "the case property." The case property was leased out to one Pearoo Mia Sardar, predecessor in interest of the present respondent Nos. 3 to 14 for a period of fifty (50) years by a registered lease deed dated 21-12-1956 by the then Mutawalli, Nawab Khawaja Habibullah which was executed with the sanction of the then Waqf Commissioner. It was stipulated in the lease deed that after expiry of the lease period in December, 2007 the lessee would hand over vacant possession of the case property to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate. The lessee had been paying rent to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate through the Mutawalli but subsequently, he became a defaulter in payment of rent. After the death of the original lessee, Pearoo Mia Sardar, his heirs who are the respondent Nos. 3 to 14 took loan from respondent No. 2, the bank and mortgaged the case property to the said bank in collusion with the bank employees concealing the fact that the case property belongs to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate. The borrowers having defaulted in payment of loan, the bank instituted Title Suit No. 244 of 1979 for recovery of outstanding loan amount against them. The Suit was decreed on compromise on 23-9-1984. But the defendant judgment-debtors having not paid the amount due to the bank in breach of the terms of the compromise, the decree holder bank put the decree on execution by filing the Title Execution Case No. 151 of 1991. The petitioner was totally ignorant of these facts till 16-1-1996 on which date he was taken by surprise to see an auction notice in the "Daily Inquilab" wherefrom he came to know that the case property was going to be sold in auction through the said Execution Case. The petitioner immediately brought it to the notice of the Managing Committee of the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate and the Managing Committee asked him to take legal steps in this respect. Accordingly, the petitioner engaged a learned Advocate, gathered information through him from the Court and obtained certified copies and came to know above facts. 

 32. After considering the facts and submissions of the parties and also considering the Writ Petition and annexure therein and the affidavit in oppositions filed by the respondents and annexure therein, it appears that the respondent No. 2 filed a suit being the Title Suit No. 244 of 1979 for recovery of loan amount of money which was decreed on compromise on 23-9-1984 in favour of the respondent No. 2, Uttara Bank Ltd. And on breach of the compromise, the Bank put the decree on execution by filing the Execution Case No. 151 of 1991 and on 16-1-96 an auction notice was published for selling the mortgaged property. It is admitted by both the parties that the said property was originally belonged to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate and the respondent No.4 to 7 are the heirs of Pearoo Miah Sarder who obtained a lease from the Waqf Estate by a Lease Deed dated 21-12-1956 executed by Nawab Khwaza Habibullah Bahadur as a Mutualli of the Dhaka Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate as a lessor. The said deed contains several terms and conditions to be fulfilled and satisfied by the lessor and by the lessee.
